Canara Bank - Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call 
14th October, 2026 
 
 
- Moderator: 
 
- …Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. Today, we have with us the senior management 
team of Canara Bank represented by –  
 
 Shri. Brajesh Kumar Singh, MD and CEO Sir 
 Shri. Hardeep Singh Ahluwalia, ED 
 Shri. Bhavendra Kumar, ED and 
 Shri. S. K. Majumdar Sir, ED. 
 
- With this, I hand over the call to the MD Sir for his opening remarks post which we will 
have a Q&A Session. Thank you and over to you, Sir. 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Thank you. Thank you there. I just welcome all our esteemed analysts to this Analyst 
Meet after having published our September quarterly results. And I am very happy to 
inform some of the salient features, though we have already provided the full Balance 
Sheet and Profit & Loss statement posted. 
 
 So, this quarter crossed a very important milestone of ₹30 lakh crores of business 
and our Total Global business stands at ₹30,72,000 crores at 15.88% YoY growth.  
 Then Global Deposit also grew by 13.13% YOY and it is as of now at ₹16,97,000 
crores. 
 Global Advances grew very robustly at 19.46% YOY, ₹13.75 lakh crores. 
 And the most heartening to note is our core business, the income from core 
business, that is Net Interest Income, grew by 20.39% and it is at ever highest YOY 
also and ever highest outstanding gross amount at ₹11,000+ crores. 
 Net Profit also grew very handsomely and it is also ever highest profit of any quarter 
at ₹5,175 crore and YOY is 8.40%. 
 CRAR is very well placed at 17.19% due to plough back also and at the same time 
density of our risk weighted asset has also improved like anything. 
 The PCR coverage also, we have increased it by 175 basis point YOY basis and now it 
stands very robustly at 95.34%. 
 Gross NPA; our total asset quality has improved like anything. Our guidance for the 
full year 31st March, 2027 was for Gross NPA 1.50 and now we have already 
improved it at 1.33%. 
 And Net NPA also we said that it will be around 0.40%. It has further improved and it 
is as of now only at 0.30%. 

 
 2
 So, if we go granularly in the Advances side, the advances growth was broad based. I 
mean, every RAM and large corporate everybody has equally contributed. To 
discuss, RAM grew by 21.03%. Within RAM; Retail Credit at 31.61%. And even we in 
Retail if we talk about Housing Loan, it has also grown 17.35%. All these numbers are 
YOY. 
 Vehicle loan grew by 25.50%. 
 If we talk about MSME also, there is a very good growth at 15.49%. 
 And in Earning Per Share also the growth is 5% and we are at ₹22.06. 
 There is an improvement of 21 basis points on YOY versus in credit cost and it is very 
handsomely placed at 0.47%. 
 And the Slippage ratio has been contained like anything and the annualized Slippage 
ratio is only 0.58% and there is an improvement of 18 basis points. 
 
- So, let me conclude by just giving you how we have fared against our guidance, which 
we gave in the start of the year. 
 
 So, we said we will grow Total Business by 10%-11%. Against that, we have grown 
15.88%. 
 Advances we said 11%-12%, we have grown 19.46%. 
 Deposit growth we said 9%-10%, now we have growth at 13.13%. 
 CASA we have said that it will be in between the range of 30%-32%, which as of now 
we are at 29%. We have protected that at 29%  in spite of the fact that we could 
garner $5.8 billion of FCNR(B) deposit, which in rupee terms is close to ₹55,000 
crores, which is all on that Term deposit. Had it not been there, we would have also 
achieved or surpassed this guidance also. Despite the Term deposit and that too in a 
very short span of time, we have still maintained it at 29%. 
 NIM, we said it will range between 2.50%-2.60%, we are at 2.53% on annual basis 
and on quarterly it is 2.55%; even better. 
 Gross NPA, I already discussed. 
 Net NPA also I discussed. 
 PCR also discussed. 
 Slippage ratio; guidance was 0.80%, now it is only at 0.58%. 
 Credit cost also I have said that we have improved and against the guidance of 
0.75% it is only 0.47%. 
 Return on Equity we said 16.5% and it is 2% more around 18.49%, to be precise. 
 Earnings Per Share also we said ₹20 and it is at ₹22.06. 
 Return on Average we said between 1.01%-1.05%, we are at 1.04%. 
 
- So, you see, barring CASA, that too I have explained why, we have surpassed by good 
margins on all the guidance. 
 
- Now, I shall be open to your analysis, your questions, any further clarification from our 
side and any guidance from your side, please.

Q&A Session 
 
- Moderator: 
 
- Thank you, Sir. We will start the Question & Answer session. Participants those who 
have any question please raise your hand. 
 
- We will take the first question from the line of Maru, please go ahead with your 
question. 
 
- Ms. Maru – Analyst: 
 
- Yeah. Hello, Sir. Good evening. Congratulations.  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Good evening, Maru. Yeah.  
 
- Ms. Maru – Analyst: 
 
- Yeah, congratulations, Sir.  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Thank you. 
 
- Ms. Maru – Analyst: 
 
- Sir, I just had a couple of questions, what would be your incremental yield on corporate 
loans currently and what would it be last quarter? As in, what was the incremental yield 
on corporate loans in the second quarter and what was it in the first quarter? And 
likewise, on Gold loans, your yields?  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Okay, that I will provide you. Yeah, we have got. Yes, let me see.  
 
- Mr. Hardeep Singh Ahluwalia – Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- The corporate the yield is 7.72% and on gold it is increased to 9.10%. It has improved 
from 8.96% to 9.10%.  
 

 
 4
- Ms. Maru – Analyst: 
 
- Okay. And corporate has improved?  
 
- Mr. Hardeep Singh Ahluwalia – Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- From 7.68% it has improved to 7.72%.  
 
- Ms. Maru – Analyst: 
 
- Okay, Sir. Got it, got it. And, Sir, what is your take on margins from here on? Do you see 
margins improve from here on too?  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- I guess we will be able to sustain this NIM at 2.55% considering, I mean, there is a rate 
hike also of 0.25 basis point. We are at 25 basis points. And our Repo rate linked book is 
53%. And again, MCLR will be also repriced but at the same time it will further depend 
upon how deposits and advances are getting repriced. But as of now, as we speak, 53% 
of book is already repriced. 
 
- And then this season there will be a lot of festivity also, so there will be a lot of 
underwriting under retail lending and growth propelled through widespread 
consumption. So, we see there is good, good margin also. 
 
- In Retail, our margin is 8.65% of our earning. So, that way it will improve. 53% already 
repriced.  
 
- Ms. Maru – Analyst: 
 
- Got it, Sir. Sir, and again on Gold loans, competition keeps increasing. I know Canara 
Bank has done well, it's one of the leaders there, but competition keeps increasing. So, 
do you see pressure on yields going ahead? Your yield has actually improved QoQ but 
do you see pressure on yield going ahead, given that competition keeps rising, even 
large NBFCs are now getting into it in a big way?  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- So, we work under a very competitive environment. So, that we are used to, I mean, 
taking on competition. So, yes. But one thing I would like to say, Gold loan we are doing 
for years all together. And I think we are very much skilled in doing Gold loans. All our 
people are very smart. We have got a very good setup of appraisers, gold safes. So, the 
whole ecosystem we have got, it is very well placed. We are market leaders also. And as 

 
 5
of now also we are not pricing very aggressively, like this NBFC and all. And we are 
always below NBFC and they can't be below us considering they borrow from us only 
and then they further go on lending. They are not a deposit taking NBFCs. 
 
- So, yes, competition is there, but we know this business, how to do this business. And 
we will be further bettering, it will be not dipping, I guess.  
 
- Ms. Maru – Analyst: 
 
- Okay, Sir, perfect. Thank you so much.  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Thank you, Maru.  
 
- Moderator: 
 
- Thank you. We will take the next question from the line of Jay Mundra. Please go ahead. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Sir, good evening, and congratulations on a steady quarter.  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Good evening, Jay. Thank you. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Good evening, Sir. Sir, a few questions. First is the bulk deposit, while we have raised 
huge FCNR(B), but it looks like that the bulk deposit has not moved either ways. I was 
under the impression that, you know, the bank may be tempted to reduce bulk deposit 
or may replace bulk by FCNR. So, what is your thought process? Can bulk deposit be 
decreased? The entire FCNR will be in Retail TD only, right? Is that understanding 
correct?  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Yeah, let me request Ahluwalia ji to answer.  
 
 
 
 

 
 6
- Mr. Hardeep Singh Ahluwalia – Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- See, Sir, last quarter we have increased the bulk and CD by ₹12,000 crores. So, from 
₹4,25,000, the bulk has gone to ₹4.37 lakh. Now, this quarter, we have consciously not 
taken and maintained at the June level from ₹4.37 lakhs to ₹4.38 lakhs. During this 
process, we have decreased the cost of deposit by 1% because the FCNR deposits were 
at 1% less than the bulk’s prevailing market price.  
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Right.  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- So, we have grown by 19% in Advances also. We have grown 13% in Deposits. So, there 
is a gap also, so it was funded there also. The part of it was utilized there.  
 
- Mr. Hardeep Singh Ahluwalia – Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- For credit. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Fully? 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Fully. 
 
- Mr. S. K. Majumdar - Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- With robust credit growth, it was utilized. No, it has replaced. What you understood was 
correct, it replaced bulk deposit. It fully replaced the bulk deposit. Otherwise, had FCNR 
not been there, bulk deposit would have been more by ₹30,000-₹35,000 crores. I mean, 
bulk CD put together.  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Yes. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Right-right, okay. And in the process, you have saved 100 basis point cost on bulk, right?

- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Yes, yes. Wherever we have replaced it, we have saved 100% . Consider it was at 6.5% 
and that was at 7.5%. Further we have saved on cost of CRR and SLR also, which is also 
22-23 point. Consider this were not supposed to be a charge CRR, SLR also. So, again, 
there is that earning also. Yeah. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Right. So, Sir, I'm not able to understand your NIM trajectory because 50% of the book 
will move up by 25 basis point immediately or it is already moved. And bulk deposit, 
even if the rate seems still softer or stable type, right. So, mathematically, the NIM 
should go up only. What is the offset?  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Okay-okay, I'll answer. This quarter, the effect of that FCNR(B) leverage will also come, 
wherein we do not have a spread of 2.55%. The spread in this, $3.2 billion, in leverage is 
only 40 basis or 50 basis points. So, that will be compensated with this. Little more, it 
will be compensated more. So, that impact will also come from this quarter know. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- OK, sure. And, Sir, in Interest Income, Interest Income on Advances, was there any one 
off? I mean, the calculated yield and even the reported yields are up by, you know, 3-4 
basis point, on the loan yield. Is there anything which helped us in improving the loan 
yields?  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- No, no, no. It is only since our average advances has continuously increased and it never 
dipped, you see. So, due to average advances on the trading side and very calibrated 
underwriting also we have done. We have not done any sub-seven loans. Rather, we 
have settled some of the sub-seven loans. And at the same time, we have settled some 
of the high cost deposit, like Mr. Ahluwalia told. 
 
- So, that's why this increased earning is there. It is merely on the count of average 
outstanding advances going one side northward only.  
 
 
 
 

 
 8
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Right, understood. And, Sir, your Gold loan, total Gold loan, in rupees crore and how 
much of that is Agri gold and Retail gold? Sir, if you have that number? 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Okay. So, ₹2.82 lakh crore is the total Gold loan. Out of which, Agriculture is ₹1.74 lakh 
crores and ₹1.08 lakhs crores is the Non-agriculture. So, all together ₹2.82 lakh crore.  
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Right. Last question, Sir, from my side is on AFS reserves. If you can quantify what was 
the AFS reserve at the end of Q1 and at the end of Q2? Yeah. 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Number I will also give but in percentage terms, I would like to say, 80%  of our 
investment book is HTM, 20%  is other than HTM - AFS and FVTPL. Out of that also 15%  
book, 15 point some odd percentage, is AFS reserve; AFS. So, even if HTM is not 
supposed to be…if you are asking about that dent of mark-to-market, so HTM is not 
supposed to be hit by MTM. But AFS is also not hitting our profit and loss. That will 
directly go to AFS reserve. Only FVTPL, which is less than 4% , around 4%, there the 
impact of mark-to-market is coming. That also I can quantify.  
 
- Mr. S. K. Majumdar - Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- Jay, you wanted to know that what is the increased loss AFS? The loss for the quarter is 
around ₹1,300 crore for the quarter in AFS. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- OK, but that is adjusted in AFS reserve, right? Nothing to do with P&L.  
 
- Mr. S. K. Majumdar - Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- Exactly. It is it is adjusted in AFS.  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Yes. 
 
 

 
 9
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Right. And, sorry, Sir, you are mentioning about the sensitivity of FVTPL.  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Yeah, FVTPL, last quarter our earning was ₹55 crore, this year… 
 
- Mr. S. K. Majumdar - Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- This year loss 55.  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- This year, loss ₹55 crore. Last quarter, earnings was around ₹500 crore, 
 
- Mr. S. K. Majumdar - Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- ₹555 crores. 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- ₹555 crores. Altogether, loss is, say, ₹600 crore. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Right. Sure, Sir. 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- That is there. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Lastly, Sir, if you can, I think I heard you on TV saying about this drought situation is not 
very problematic as of now. But are you seeing anything that can reduce your recovery 
efforts even in those affected district? How can that pan out? I mean, if you can… 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Not much. 3 states have been declared drought-affected. 
 

 
 10
- Mr. Hardeep Singh Ahluwalia – Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- Part of Karnataka, then Maharashtra. These 2 states are only affected, that too part. 
There will not be much effect on the recovery because restructuring is happening 
through SLBC.  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Total exposure to drought-prone area is around ₹10,000 crore to ₹13,000 crore. 
 
- Mr. Hardeep Singh Ahluwalia – Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- ₹13,900. 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- That will not affect much. ₹13,900 some odd amount. Again, some dispensation also will 
come from SLBC side. That has already come. We’ll sell through that, I guess. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Right. So, Sir, these amount, let’s say ₹13,000-₹14,000 crore, that will be restructured, 
right? Or can be restructured? 
 
- Mr. S. K. Majumdar - Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- Absolutely 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Yes. Restructured, or deferment is there, moratorium is there, some restructuring, some 
additional support also it comes. It is decided state by state by State Level Bankers’ 
Committee. 
 
- Mr. S. K. Majumdar - Executive Director, Canara Bank: 
 
- SLBC has already helped. 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 11
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- And like last to last quarter, emergency line of credit was there, so that helped. Some 
kind of dispensation every time comes. This will be also not an exception, you see. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Right-right. No, Sir, my worry is by the time dispensation come, can these account 
become NPA or they will be straightaway restructured?  
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- So, like I've said, there is no stress in my book going further also. Even if you take SMA 0 
into consideration, total stress is only 2.42%. Slippages also last quarter were only 
0.15%. That way we do not see or perceive any stress in our book. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Right. This 2.4% is all ticket size, right, including below ₹5 crore also? 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Every ticket. Yes-yes. If you talk about more than ₹5 crore, then it is less than 1%; 0.30% 
only. 
 
- Mr. Jay Mundra – Analyst: 
 
- Right-right. Okay, Sir. Great and thank you and all the very best. 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Thank you. Thank you, Jay. 
 
- Moderator: 
 
- Thank you. We will take the next question from the line of Sushil Choksey. Please go 
ahead. 
 
- Mr. Sushil Choksey – Analyst: 
 
-  Sir, congratulations to Team Canara on excellent performance. 
 
 

 
 12
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Thank you, Choksey Sahab. 
 
- Mr. Sushil Choksey – Analyst: 
 
- First question to you, Sir. Your key ratio table, page number...I have heard whatever you 
have replied to Maru and Jay Mundra. 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Yeah. 
 
- Mr. Sushil Choksey – Analyst: 
 
- So, I have a specific question. As you are saying, there is no stress, margins have 
bottomed out, your efforts on saving CASA is looking good, irrespective of FCNR deposit 
taking up the toll. Would you like to revise your guidance for the year on any 
parameters starting from ROA, ROE, cost to income, CD or any of the parameters? 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- Like I said, Sir, these were all decided before my joining the bank, and we are just 
respecting that. I said, I will work hard, team will work hard, we will better it. You have 
seen everywhere we have already bettered it, and we will sustain it. I said, instead of 
going and revising my own guidance, let me better it. We are bettering it only. We are 
not restricting ourself anywhere, we are not sticking to guidance. You see, against 
Advances growth of 11%-12%, we are booking 19%. We are just concentrating ourself to 
let this growth story be a very sustainable one. So, we have no plan to evaluate, Sir. 
Yeah. 
 
- Mr. Sushil Choksey – Analyst: 
 
- Sir, as of October 14th, what is the visibility on RAM business being festive quarter and 
Karnataka has a big festive, pretty specifically around Dussehra? 
 
- Second thing, how is your Gold loan business looking? 
 
- How is your corporate pipeline looking and overall business mix? How do you see 
visibility for Canara for the quarter and for the year?

- Specifically, looking at the businesses which are emerging in state of Karnataka and 
Tamil Nadu, where we have a good concentrate, manufacturing business are expanding. 
Be it Auto, be it Defense, many other such businesses are emerging out of these two 
states, so how is the new business segment emerging for you where the credit is likely 
to do well? 
 
- Mr. Brajesh Kumar Singh - MD & CEO, Canara Bank: 
 
- So, first question, Sir, we are seeing very robust demand for retail lending products. Our 
Housing loan in excess of 17%, 18% is growing. Total retail, 21%, vehicle loan, 25%. It is a 
very good demand also, that too without this festive season. We have already started 
getting those numbers. We are already in the festive mode. 
 
- Yes, our presence is very good in the state of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and 
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana also. What benefit we get due to this presence, and since 
we are born here only, that we are very well-recognized. That branding issue is not 
there, and we are kind of first choice bank here. That benefit we are already getting. 
 
- And this quarter, due to this festivity and others, like Governor Sahab also you would 
have seen, in spite of him raising Repo rate by 25 basis points, he revised the growth 
projections for the country from 6.7% to 7.1%, 40 basis points. That way, country is also 
very resilient and robust, and we do not see any stress in our books also. We see that 
this quarter, going further, will be a good quarter. 
 
- Again, regarding pipeline of large corporate book or mid corporate book you asked. So, 
altogether, already sanctioned not disbursed, and we have got good hot leads in hand. 
That is around ₹47,000 crore. Let’s say, around, in and out, ₹50,000 crore. 
 
- And in June also, similar kind of pipeline was there. I guess, there is a sustained demand 
also from the market, most particularly from power sector, green sector, power 
evacuation, battery storage, data centers. Many, Sir. From infrastructure also. There is a 
good pipeline, I can say. That ₹50,000 crore is in my hand only. 
 
- And RAM is also doing good, Sir. 
 
- Mr. Sushil Choksey – Analyst: 
 
- Sir, my next question is, how is outlook for recovery from written off accounts? Second 
thing is on your subsidiaries. And third is, treasury, you will have a painful time, how are 
we weathering the storm where treasury is concerned? So, if you can highlight more on 
your subsidiaries and the written off accounts.

- Okay, Sir. I will start with the recovery part. Recovery, though, there is no challenge as 
such. In percentage basis, we are recovering very handsome. Every quarter, we are 
recovering more than what we are slipping. This quarter was also not an exception. That 
is one.

dwindling down. All those Gross advances also, you have seen, it is only 1.33%. In the 
total absolute terms also, it is around ₹18,000 crore only. Part of it is already resolved 
and recovered also. And some of the outstandings are in our book only due to CIRP or 
PPIRP processes. That pool is dwindling down, and we are not slipping also very heavily 
in the new slippages; only 0.15% quarter. That pool is this. 
 
- So, in absolute term, recovery will be not as much as what we are recovering as of now. 
But, yes, 1-2 quarters, there is absolutely no issue. But going further, that very pool is 
dwindling down. One thing. But there will be another benefits, if we are not slipping, 
then what we will recover. That is one thing. 
 
- Then the next question you asked, Sir, regarding? 
 
- Mr. Sushil Choksey – Analyst: 
 
- Subsidiaries.

- Subsidiaries. 
 
- Mr. Sushil Choksey – Analyst: 
 
- Insurance and-

them. They are all good, profit earning, and their share/stock is also doing good. Canara
